claim: Name resolution behaves exactly as listed: missing/empty name means the reserved `default` profile; a name failing the 1-64 character `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` identifier check in `validate_profile_name` raises `ProfileNameError` before the agent runs; a valid name with no stored profile falls back to the stored `default`; with no stored `default` every field comes from the base config.

- A missing or empty name means the reserved `default` profile.
- A name that is not a valid identifier (1 to 64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, checked by `validate_profile_name`) raises `ProfileNameError` before the agent runs.
- A valid name with no stored profile falls back to the stored `default` profile.
- If there is no stored `default` profile, every field comes from the base config.

claim: The refusal-redaction entry in docs/internal/glossary.md describes only behavior RefusalRedactingRunner actually performs, and claims nothing about an RLS scope-analysis failure reason being logged nowhere.
source_excerpt: - **Refusal redaction** — While a rule-set file is configured, `RefusalRedactingRunner` in `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` replaces the text of each guard refusal that reaches it with the refusal's kind. A `RuleSetRefusal` is passed on unchanged, because `RuleSetGuardRunner` has already logged it. For every other refusal, the redactor logs one WARNING line. That line includes the refusal's full text, unless the refusal was raised from an error that is not itself a refusal. In that case, `_logged_by_guard` treats the error as already logged with a traceback by the guard's fail-closed path, so the redactor's line carries only the kind.
verify_against: RefusalRedactingRunner and _logged_by_guard in src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py, plus the RlsError re-raise in RlsGuardRunner (src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py)
verify_hint: Check src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py around the RefusalRedactingRunner WARNING log and `_logged_by_guard`, and the RlsError wrap in RlsGuardRunner in src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py
prior_evidence: The first half matches the code. rule_sets.py:1005-1013 logs one WARNING per refusal, with the full text only when `_logged_by_guard` is false. `_logged_by_guard` (971-980) is false when the cause is None, UnsafeSqlError or RlsError. The second half is false. rls.py has no logging. Scope-analysis failure raises RlsError at rls.py:271 from the traverse_scope exception, with the reason in the message. The only caller of apply_rls is RlsGuardRunner (safety/__init__.py:199, wired in agent/factory.py:128). It catches RlsError at 206-212 and re-raises RlsError(f'...could not be applied: {e}') from e, so the new exception's cause is an RlsError. In the redactor, `_logged_by_guard` is therefore False, and line 1013 logs `exc`, whose text includes the full scope-analysis reason. The reason is logged by the redactor, so 'logged nowhere' is a counterexample. The glossary line (docs/internal/glossary.md:27) states a false behavior. The 'every guard refusal' wording is also loose: RuleSetRefusal is re-raised unredacted at 1002-1004.

claim: The load-failure bullets in docs/internal/setup/profiles.md hold for every input ProfileStore._read_from_disk can see, including an entry whose body is not a JSON object alongside an invalid profile name.
source_excerpt: - A single entry that fails validation is skipped and logged on its own line. When every entry name is valid, `load_error` names every skipped entry.
verify_hint: Trace src/sqllens/profiles.py lines ~138-209 (_flag_corrupt, the skipped-entry branches, the invalid-name branch and the _save refusal) against the three bullets at docs/internal/setup/profiles.md:60-62
prior_evidence: Most of the claim holds in src/sqllens/profiles.py. Lines 138-152: OSError, invalid JSON and a non-dict top level each call _flag_corrupt, which sets a 'Warning:' load_error, logs it and returns with no profiles. Nothing deletes the file. Lines 180-189: a bad-name entry sets _invalid_profile_names, and load_error carries only the count. Lines 204-209: _save raises when that flag is set, and upsert and delete both go through _save. Lines 190-202: when all names are valid, load_error names every skipped entry. The claim breaks at lines 165-167. An entry whose body is not a JSON object (e.g. {"a": "str"}) is appended to `skipped` with no logger call. Only the ValidationError branch (lines 170-178) logs a per-entry line. The doc says every skipped entry is 'logged on its own line' and that bad-body entries are 'named only in their per-entry log lines' when a bad name is also present. For a non-object body alongside a bad name, the entry is never named anywhere: load_error gives only the count and there is no per-entry log. So the doc is wrong for that input.
